newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 7.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Two months into the financial year, the cabinet will already have to cut about 11 billion crowns from it's expenditure. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik made this decision after discovering that by the end of February, the state had collected almost seven billion crowns less in taxes than it should have.
- A commercial court announced the bankruptcy of Poldi Steel on Tuesday.

- Beseda Holding, which has loose ties with Nova television, bought the daily newspaper Telegraf from Intergra. The co-owner of Beseda Holding is Beseda, which publishes the magasine TV Nova Ano and organises Klub Planeta Nova, as well as the monthly Cago Belo, Silenci.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The agricultural sector in 1996 probably broke even, according to an estimate from the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU). According to Josef Hrbek, the director of agricultural economics at the CSU, there could either be profits of 100 million crowns or a loss of the same amount.
- According to the expectations of the chairman of the Christian Democratic Union, Josef Lux, the cabinet should approve material for government aid for new housing construction.
- On Monday, the administrative council of Czech Railways will decide on accepting the resignation of the general director of Czech Railways, Rudolf Mladek.

- Motoinvest became the largest shareholder of Spolchemie. The director of Motoinvest, Pavel Tykac, stated that Motoinvest will not own Spolchemie for very long, and that it is prepared to sell it to the other shareholders.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The committee for trade on the Prague Stock Exchange presented a list of 492 share issues which will be delisted during March. The first 100 issues will leave the exchange on March 20, and the remaining 392 shares will be taken out on April 1.
- Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus met with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok yesterday in Prague. The ministers discussed the Czech trade deficit and the Czech Republic's possible entry into the EU.
PRAVO - The chairman of the railway workers union, Jaromir Dusek, said yesterday after a meeting of Czech union chairmen that announcing another strike is an acute possibility.
- Foreign travel for parliamentary representatives cost the parliamentary budget nearly three million crowns in the first two months of this year.
